title: Batch renaming files using item enumeration when the new name already exists causes unexpected behavior
author: tiosolid
summary: PowerRename executes an enumerated rename chain directly into names still occupied by other selected files, causing Explorer-style '(2)' collision suffixes.

confidence.rationale: The collision graph and direct-execution mechanism fit the deterministic result; staging is a standard general solution for rename chains and cycles.

judgment.rationale: The deterministic file set and replacement pattern directly establish a same-directory rename dependency chain. Prior focused investigation identified single-pass shell rename execution without staging.
evidence: Renaming bill-01 through bill-11 to bill-02 through bill-12 produces '(2)' suffixes.
Every desired target except the last is initially occupied by another selected source file.
The PowerRename worker has been observed queuing direct shell RenameItem operations without a dependency graph or temporary-name staging pass.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a bounded design for dependency-aware or two-phase same-directory rename execution.

fix_assessment.rationale: No active merged fix covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path. This is a strong design candidate: build a per-directory rename graph, stage blocking/cyclic sources to unique temporary names, then apply final names while preserving existing depth ordering and error reporting.

proposed_fixes.title: Stage overlapping PowerRename targets before final rename
proposed_fixes.root_cause: PowerRename directly renames each selected item to its desired name while another selected source still occupies that path, so shell collision handling appends '(2)'.
plan: Build a case-insensitive per-directory map of current and desired paths before executing renames.
Stage items participating in blocking chains or cycles to unique same-directory temporary names, then rename staged items to their final names.
Preserve parent/child depth ordering, update item bookkeeping after each pass, and add chain/swap/partial-failure tests.
verification: Run the bill-01 through bill-11 shift and verify exact bill-02 through bill-12 output with no suffixes.
Run a two-file swap and a case-only rename to verify cycles and Windows path semantics.
